card.keepWhy: She won him every day, not in one big day.
sources: Shiva Purana, Rudra Samhita, Parvati Khanda (Parvati’s tapas to win Shiva; Shiva comes disguised as a young ascetic, speaks against himself to test her, and reveals himself)
Kalidasa, Kumarasambhava, canto 5 (Parvati’s tapas; the young ascetic’s test); 5.28: she gave up even fallen leaves, so she is called Aparna
tapas: literally heat; steady, disciplined spiritual effort
check: The film calls the disguised Shiva “a young wanderer”; the texts say a young brahmachari (student-ascetic). Confirm acceptable.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there something big you want? a skill, a goal, a dream that won’t come overnight.
options: then this story is for you. listen.
then pick one while you listen.
good. keep this one for when you do.

steps.line: Parvati wanted to marry Shiva, the great yogi. But he was lost in meditation, and noticed no one.

steps.q: Before Parvati tries anything, the gods send Kama, the god of love, to shoot Shiva with a flower arrow. What happens?
o: Shiva falls for Parvati on the spot
His third eye burns Kama to ash
The arrow glances off; Kama flees
steps.why: One look from his third eye, and the love god was ash. So Parvati chose another way: not a trick, but a practice of her own.

steps.line: So she began her own practice.
Day after day, season after season, through heat and rain, she meditated in the mountains.
steps.label: tapas

steps.q: Hindus call her kind of practice tapas. What does the word first mean?
steps.why: Tapas means heat: the inner fire that steady effort builds. In the old stories, great tapas could make even the gods feel the warmth.

steps.q: A young wanderer mocks Shiva: why waste your life on him? What do you think Parvati does?
o: Starts to doubt, and asks him more
steps.why: She defends him, hard. Watch who he really is.

steps.line: One day a young wanderer came by and mocked Shiva. Why waste your life on him?
Parvati defended Shiva so fiercely that the young man smiled. He was Shiva himself, in disguise, testing her.

steps.q: The gods were cheering Parvati on. Why did they need this marriage?
o: Only a son of Shiva could defeat a demon
To bring the rains back to the mountains
So Shiva would rule over the gods
steps.why: The demon Taraka could be beaten only by a son of Shiva. Their son, Kartikeya, was born for that, as Kalidasa’s poem Kumarasambhava tells.

steps.line: Her steady practice had won him. What you want, you build, day by day.
steps.label: today

steps.q: In Kalidasa’s famous poem, Shiva drops his disguise with a surprising line. What does he say?
o: You have passed. Now you may be my bride.
From today, I am your servant, bought by your tapas.
Rest now, my love. Your practice is complete.
steps.why: Kalidasa’s word is krita, bought: “From today I am your servant, bought by your tapas.” The great yogi didn’t claim her; her practice won him.

say: here’s what i love. parvati didn’t win shiva in one big day. she won him every day, season after season.
hindus honor tapas, steady practice that changes the one who does it. her practice changed her as much as it moved him.

steps.q: In one famous telling, Parvati practiced so hard she stopped eating even leaves, and was called Aparna. Parna means leaf. What does Aparna mean?
o: The one who eats only leaves
The one without even a leaf
steps.why: A-parna: without a leaf. Her name holds how far her practice went.

today.say: choose one thing you’ll practice every day this week, even for five minutes. that’s your tapas. many hindus begin a practice with a short prayer to shiva and parvati. you can learn one, join in, or just begin. it’s your choice.
options: then day one is today. parvati’s way.
so has everyone. season after season means starting again too.
